The Zipf exponent is calculated by fitting a power law to the rank-frequency distribution. The formula is:

rank ∝ frequency^(-α)

frequency ∝ rank^(-1/α)

For the Zipf exponent, we typically:

2. Assign ranks (1, 2, 3, ...)
3. Fit log(rank) vs log(frequency) to a linear model
4. The slope gives -1/α, so α = -1/slope

# Method: Zipf exponent calculation using linear regression on log-log

# log(rank) = a - (1/alpha) * log(frequency)
# slope = -1/alpha, so alpha = -1/slope

ranks = list(range(1, len(sorted_values) + 1))

# Alternative method: Maximum likelihood estimator for Zipf's law

print(f"MLE Zipf exponent rounded to nearest thousandth = {round(alpha_mle, 3)}")
